subject: Usage-mapped GPU retargeting plan for StrataWare renewal
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@strataware.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@strataware.com
Date: Mon, 24 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in inference usage — need options ahead of renewal

Hi Logan / Ben,

Quick note from our side: over the last 4 weeks we've seen sustained 2.8x higher peak token throughput on the production routes tied to our conversational assistant (mainly daytime PST). We've attached the utilization export (CSV) — you'll see the pattern: predictable diurnal peaks but also a couple of multi-hour sustained bursts.

Our renewal is coming up in 6 weeks (May 31). We need to understand:
- Can we add short-term GPUs while we renegotiate the commit?
- If we move to a larger committed tranche, what is the sizing recommendation based on the attached usage?
- Pricing / SLA implications for an interim top-up vs a permanent tranche increase.

We prefer a predictable monthly cost if possible, but can't risk product degradation next month. Can we schedule a 30-min runbook call today or tomorrow?

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Platform, StrataWare

Attachments: 20280424_strataware_utilization_report.csv (CSV, 32 KB)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@strataware.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in inference usage — need options ahead of renewal

Hi Aisha — thanks for the export and the head's up. We saw the same patterns in our telemetry and pulled a quick analysis. High level answer first, details below:

Short answer: two viable paths
1) Burst/top-up pool (short lead, low friction) — add 8 A100-equivalent GPUs to a burst pool for 30 days while we finalize commitment sizing.
2) Commit retargeting (longer-term, better unit economics) — increase committed tranche by an equivalent of 6 steady GPUs with an option to auto-burst on peaks. This smooths cost and gives better per-token pricing.

Sizing rationale (summary):
- Your 95th percentile sustained token throughput maps to ~5.5 GPUs sustained under current model mix and sequence lengths.
- Peaks (95->99.5) require ~11 GPUs for 3-5 hour bursts.
- We recommend committing to 6 GPUs (covers sustained baseline + 1 buffer) and keeping an 8-GPU burst pool for the predictable peak windows. That gives you headroom without overcommit.

Operational notes:
- Burst pool can be provisioned within 24h with Dedicated Addendum; pricing is usage-based and billed pro rata.
- Commit retargeting requires a quick amendment to the Dedicated contract (SOW addendum). If signed by May 3 we can schedule capacity and avoid throttling during renewal.
- We can also apply workload-level optimizations (batching window adjustments, adaptive KV cache TTLs) that lower peak GPU needs ~8-12% depending on traffic shape. Engineering (Ben) can scope the work in the call.

I've attached a draft SOW addendum (SOW_v1_StrataWare_GPU_addendum.pdf) to show the two pricing scenarios side-by-side. Can you do 30 minutes at 11:30am PST today? If not, tomorrow morning works as well.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0192

Attachments: SOW_v1_StrataWare_GPU_addendum.pdf (PDF, 48 KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@strataware.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in inference usage — need options ahead of renewal

On Mon, Apr 24, 2028 at 10:05 Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Aisha — thanks for the export and the head's up. We saw the same patterns in our telemetry and pulled a quick analysis.
> 
> Short answer: two viable paths
> 1) Burst/top-up pool (short lead, low friction) — add 8 A100-equivalent GPUs to a burst pool for 30 days while we finalize commitment sizing.

Quick technical note from infra: the utilization CSV shows a high fraction of long sequences on route /chat-core between 10:00-15:00 PST. Before we spin up extra hardware, Karthik suggests a two-hour experiment to enable condensed batching + dynamic KV pruning on a staging slice of traffic. If that reduces consumed GPU slots by ~10% we can defer 2 GPUs from the burst plan.

Also flagging: if StrataWare wants the burst pool isolated (separate tenant) we need to run a quick security checklist; that adds ~2 business days to provisioning. If shared pool is okay, we can do same-day.

I'll prep the test runbook and a quick ops checklist for the call.

- Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@strataware.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@strataware.com
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in inference usage — need options ahead of renewal

Thanks — that all makes sense. We can do the following next steps: 
1) Approve the 30-day burst pool of 8 GPUs on a shared tenant while Redwood runs the two-hour batching experiment (please send an order link).
2) If the experiment yields >8% reduction, we cap the burst to 6 GPUs and the procurement team will review the SOW addendum for committing to +6 GPUs permanently.
3) Procurement needs a quoted price for both scenarios (30-day burst; +6 committed GPUs) and an SLA clarification for the committed tranche (latency SLO and scheduled maintenance windows).

Call confirmed for tomorrow 11:30am PST. Logan — please send the DocuSign/Order link for the burst pool and the revised SOW reflecting the shared-pool option. Ben — look forward to the test runbook and ops checklist.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Aisha Khan
Head of Platform, StrataWare

Quoted attachments in thread: 20280424_strataware_utilization_report.csv (attached), SOW_v1_StrataWare_GPU_addendum.pdf (attached)
